title: Evaluating the Role of Interoperability in Dentistry: A Mixed-Methods Assessment of EHR Maturity in Germany
summary: This study examines how well dental record systems in Germany are able to share and reuse information in a standardized way, which is becoming increasingly important under new European rules for health data exchange. It will look at which standards already exist for dental documentation, how much information in dental records is entered in a structured format versus written as free text, and what currently prevents better communication between systems. To do this, the study combines a review of existing standards, an analysis of fully anonymized dental record data to determine how consistently clinical information can be translated into a common standardized format, and a Delphi survey with relevant stakeholders to identify obstacles and develop practical recommendations for improving interoperability in dentistry.
conditions: This study does not address a specific disease or health condition. Instead, it focuses on the interoperability of dental electronic health records and the standardized documentation of oral health information.

Inclusion criteria:
In the second phase, this study will use anonymized retrospective patient data which will be randomly selected and exported from the hospital EHR system. While it is assumed that most included patients will be adults, the inclusion of children is possible (but not explicitly targeted).

None.
